title: Dynamic <sup>1</sup> H-MRS for detection of <sup>13</sup> C-labeled glucose metabolism in the human brain at 3T.
abstract: PURPOSE: In 2004, Boumezbeur et al proposed a simple yet powerful approach to detect the metabolism of <sup>13</sup> C-enriched substrates in the brain. Their approach consisted of dynamic <sup>1</sup> H-MRS, without a <sup>13</sup> C radiofrequency (RF) channel, and its successful application was demonstrated in monkeys. Since then, this promising method has yet to be applied rigorously in humans. In this study, we revisit the use of dynamic <sup>1</sup> H-MRS to measure the metabolism of <sup>13</sup> C-enriched substrates and demonstrate its application in the human brain. METHODS: In healthy participants, <sup>1</sup> H-MRS data were acquired dynamically before and following a bolus infusion of [1-<sup>13</sup> C] glucose. Data were acquired on a 3T clinical MRI scanner using a short-TE SPECIAL sequence, with regions of interest in both anterior and posterior cingulate cortex. Using simulated basis spectra to model signal changes in both <sup>12</sup> C-bonded and <sup>13</sup> C-coupled resonances, the acquired spectra were fit in LCModel to obtain labeling time courses for glutmate and glutamine at both C4 and C3 positions. RESULTS: Presence of the <sup>13</sup> C label was clearly detectable, owing to the pronounced effect of heteronuclear (<sup>13</sup> C-<sup>1</sup> H) scalar coupling on the observed <sup>1</sup> H spectra. A decrease in signal from <sup>12</sup> C-bonded protons and an increase in signal from <sup>13</sup> C-coupled protons were observed. The fractional enrichment of Glu-C4, (Glu+Gln)-C4, and (Glu+Gln)-C3 at 30 minutes following infusion of [1-<sup>13</sup> C] glucose was similar in both regions: 11% to 13%, 9% to 12% and 3% to 5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: These preliminary results confirm the feasibility of the use of dynamic <sup>1</sup> H-MRS to monitor <sup>13</sup> C labeling in the human brain, without a <sup>13</sup> C RF channel.
